scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service charge incurred 34 days ago, which is slightly outside the standard 30-day refund window policy.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Soo-ah Kim and I'm 42. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?

Hello Soo-ah, thank you for reaching out. I understand how frustrating it can be to return from travel and find an unexpected charge. I would be happy to look into this for you. To get started, could you please provide your account number and the email address associated with your subscription?
Sure, my account number is 8849201 and the email is sooah.k@email.com.

Thank you, Soo-ah. I have located your account. For security, could you please confirm the last four digits of the payment method on file and the date the cancellation request was originally submitted?
The card ends in 4492, and I believe I clicked the cancel button on the website on October 12th.

I appreciate that verification. I see the cancellation request logged on October 12th. While our 'Service Agreement Section 4.2' strictly mandates refund requests be submitted within 30 days of the charge date, I can see you were a loyal subscriber for two years prior to this. Given the circumstances of your travel, I am authorized to make a one-time exception to this policy.
Oh, that would be such a relief. Thank you so much for understanding!

You are very welcome. I have successfully processed a full refund of $49.99 to your card ending in 4492. You should see the credit appear in your account within 3-5 business days depending on your bank's processing time. Is there anything else I can assist you with today?

resolution_summary: The agent verified the account and the cancellation date, then exercised authorized discretion to grant a one-time policy exception for a refund request that was 4 days past the 30-day limit.
